title: Regression snippetbook — short experiments and quick rubrics
text:
Context / purpose:
----
Quick scratchpad for a few odd regressions I ran into while validating v1.8 quant rollout on staging. Goal: capture small reproducible prompts, ad-hoc scoring rubric I used for fast triage, and immediate hypotheses + actions. Not a formal postmortem — more of a personal lab notebook to save time next run.

High-level summary (short):
- Symptoms: occasional short-output truncation + mild repetition starting ~token 20 on some instruction prompts; increased hallucination for list-style instructions on v1.8-quant vs v1.7-fp16.
- Affects: small subset of prompts that request multi-step lists or enumerated items (~5–12% of test sample).
- Suspected cause(s): quantization noise shifting token logits near end of first prefix span; KV-cache alignment differences; or compiler kernel choice for small batch sizes.

Ad-hoc rubric (used for rapid scoring, 1–5 where 5 is best):
- Coherence (1–5): does the response make sense throughout?
- Completeness (1–5): does it answer all sub-steps?
- Repetition (1–5): 5 == no repetition, 1 == strong loop/repeat
- Hallucination (1–5): factual fabrications / invented facts
- Latency/Throughput note (N/A or short): whether the variant materially slows down the run

Test harness notes:
- Small batch size (batch=1, stream off) to see per-request behavior.
- Temperature=0.2, top_p=0.95.
- Compare: rwd-v1.7-fp16 (baseline) vs rwd-v1.8-quant (staging) vs rwd-v1.8-quant-er (experimental kernel).
- Seeded sampling for deterministic-ish compare (seed=42).

Representative prompt + raw outputs (trimmed):
Prompt A (instruction):
"Write a step-by-step checklist for onboarding a new engineer to a backend service team. Include 8 concrete tasks and suggested duration for each."

Baseline (v1.7-fp16) — observed: clean, 8 items listed, small elaboration:
- Score: Coherence 5 / Completeness 5 / Repetition 5 / Hallucination 5
- Example line: "(3) Setup local dev: clone repo, run docker-compose up, run unit tests — ~2 hours"

v1.8-quant — observed: stops after item 4, then repeats variations of item 2, slight token-level loop around dev setup step:
- Score: Coherence 3 / Completeness 2 / Repetition 2 / Hallucination 4
- Noted artifact: truncation occurs at token ~78 in our tokenizer count; loop begins immediately after.

v1.8-quant-er (alt kernel) — observed: completes list but two items collapsed into one (counts 7 unique items) and one item is terse:
- Score: Coherence 4 / Completeness 3 / Repetition 4 / Hallucination 4

Small sample of other prompts where behavior appears:
- Prompt B: "Give 6 troubleshooting steps to diagnose 500 errors in a microservice" — v1.8-quant sometimes duplicates step 3.
- Prompt C: "Enumerate 10 security checklist items for onboarding an external vendor" — v1.8-quant truncates at 6–7 items.

Quick hypotheses (ranked):
1) Quantization-induced logit noise biases probability mass early, causing early beam collapse on enumerated outputs.
2) Kernel path chosen for sequences <128 tokens has an off-by-one in cache advancing leading to repetition after certain token alignment.
3) Temperature/top-p interplay with quantized logits increases chance of short-loop token choices.

Rapid experiments to run (next 24–48h):
- Re-run Prompt A with forced max_new_tokens=160 to confirm whether truncation is genuine or stop-token misfire. (TODO)
- Run same prompts with batch size 4 to see if batching/continuous-batching changes kernel selection. (TODO)
- Try disabling KV caching in runtime for a quick test to observe if repetition disappears. (TODO: RWD-879)
- Run calibration sweep of quantization scale on last 10 layers (local edge case test).

Quick mitigation ideas (fast):
- For prod rollout, gate quantized model behind canary with payloads that include enumerative tasks. If failing rate > 5% on that cohort, rollback.
- Add a short post-process check: if response repeats token sequences or stops early in list prompts, trigger fallback to higher-fidelity variant. Cheap guardrail in RD code path.

Notes to self / annotations:
- Keep examples minimal — long essays aren't affected. Seems specific to enumerative outputs (lists).
- Check commit that changed int8 kernel switch - PR #612 may have introduced differing kernel selection rules (linked above).
- Luca: asked about adding a short unit test that synthesizes repetition signature — follow up in sync.

Raw scoring table (first pass: 25 samples, quick eyeball):
- Baseline average completeness: 4.6
- v1.8-quant average completeness: 3.1
- v1.8-quant-er average completeness: 3.7
- Actionable threshold: completeness drop > 0.8 triggers rollback for a major customer cohort.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is the behavior correlated with specific tokenizers (we use same tokenizer but different kernel may use sub-token pack heuristics)?
- Are certain prompt patterns (explicit numbers like "8 tasks") more fragile than open-ended list prompts?
- Does high latency in one shard increase chance of repetition due to request retry/fallback?

Immediate next notes (this doc is a scratchpad):
- Re-run with deterministic decoding (greedy) to see if sampling amplifies the spike.
- Add a short test harness script to repo tests/regressions/list-loop-check.py that runs a set of 50 enumerative prompts across model variants and outputs quick CSV (prompt id, model, completeness, repetition_score).
- If pattern holds, coordinate with release-engineering to hold canary.

Very short TL;DR to paste into channel: "Quick heads-up: v1.8-quant shows list truncation/repetition on ~10% of enumerative prompts vs v1.7. Running tiny triage; hypothesize quantization/kernel selection. Will run batch and kv-cache disable experiments and report back by EOD Fri."

End of notebook. Notes are chaotic — meant for fast follow-up rather than polished documentation.
